title: Why the last part of your iPhone charge slows down
script: Why does the last twenty percent take forever? You plug in your iPhone, watch it climb, then the finish line starts crawling. Here's what's happening. Early in a normal charge, the battery can accept a higher current. As its voltage reaches the charging limit, the charger holds that voltage and eases the current down. Less current means those last few percent arrive more slowly. But an iPhone sitting at eighty percent overnight can be doing something else. Optimized Battery Charging learns your routine and may wait to finish until you're about to unplug. Heat can limit charging too. So a slow finish and a deliberate pause can look similar. Your phone is managing the battery, even when you're staring at the number. Follow TechWhoKnows for more everyday tech explained.

claim_ledger.claim: Apple charging slows after about80%, timing depends on device/settings.
General lithium-ion constant-voltage phase reduces current at regulation voltage. Not an iPhone IC teardown.
Optimized Battery Charging may delay past80% in an expected long charging session.
Warmth can limit charging. Not every slowdown is heat.
